study_audits.study_design: mixed methods intervention study: pre/post/delayed writing tests plus questionnaires and focus groups

control_group.note: Comparison group of 56 students received traditional writing instruction without ChatGPT.

randomization.note: No random assignment; group allocation raises self-selection risk.

transfer_test.note: No independent no-AI writing transfer test; all outcomes measured while ChatGPT usage was part of the condition.

sample_bias.note: Final analysis 35 EG + 37 CG (72) from 78 + 56 initial enrolments.

self_selection.note: Consent-based participation; students may self-select into the experimental group.

measurement_validity.note: Rubric-scored writing tests with pre/post/delayed structure, triangulated by questionnaires and focus groups.

confounders.note: Novelty effect and single-institution context not controlled.

instructor_effect.note: Single institution; instructor assignment across groups not detailed.

novelty_effect.note: 6-hour intervention is very short; novelty likely inflates perceived benefit.

ai_usage_policy.note: ChatGPT deployed as a formative feedback tool, but precise usage boundaries are not fully specified.

dropout.note: Attrition from 78/56 to 35/37 final analysed; reasons not detailed.

task_vs_learning_guard.measured_construct: rubric-scored writing test performance in a formative-feedback condition
task_vs_learning_guard.note: Improved writing scores may partly reflect AI-supported task performance rather than independent writing ability; without a no-AI independent writing assessment, writing score gain cannot be equated with independent writing skill gain.

limitations: No independent no-AI writing transfer test
Attrition between initial and final samples not fully explained
suggestions: Extend intervention duration to a full term
Add an independent no-AI writing transfer assessment
Report dropout reasons and usage-fidelity data

study_audits.study_design: large-scale three-arm randomized controlled trial (no AI / GPT Base unguarded / GPT Tutor guardrailed)

post_test.note: Practice performance and independent exam measured.

transfer_test.note: Independent closed-book exam functions as a transfer check from practice, but no longer-term transfer measure.

measurement_validity.note: Independent exam without AI access cleanly separates task performance from learning.

confounders.note: Three-arm design isolates the effect of tool design.

instructor_effect.note: Standardized study sessions; instructor effects minimized.

novelty_effect.note: Short in-class sessions; novelty not explicitly controlled.

ai_usage_policy.note: Explicit contrast between unguarded (GPT Base) and guardrailed (GPT Tutor) usage.

dropout.note: Not reported in the reviewed summary.

task_vs_learning_guard.measured_construct: practice problem performance vs independent closed-book exam performance
task_vs_learning_guard.note: The study itself demonstrates the dissociation: +48%/+127% practice performance coexisted with -17% independent exam performance in the unguarded arm.

limitations: Subject mismatch: high school mathematics, not university academic writing
No positive learning gain even with guardrails (they eliminate harm, do not produce gain)
suggestions: Replicate the guardrail design in a writing context

study_audits.study_design: randomized controlled trial across four high school ESL classes comparing GPT-4 interactive homework with traditional homework

randomization.note: Randomized controlled trial at class level.

pre_test.note: Baseline learning levels measured; detail limited in the reviewed summary.

post_test.note: Learning outcome assessments and engagement measures collected.

sample_bias.note: Four classes only; modest sample, clustering at class level.

measurement_validity.note: Learning outcomes measured in addition to engagement, not only task performance.

confounders.note: Class-level clustering and possible platform differences between homework modes.

instructor_effect.note: Four classes; instructor differences across classes not fully controlled.

novelty_effect.note: Novel interactive platform may inflate engagement.

ai_usage_policy.note: Interactive homework tutor design defined, but guardrail details limited in the reviewed summary.

dropout.note: Not reported in the reviewed summary.

task_vs_learning_guard.measured_construct: homework task completion/engagement vs ESL learning outcome assessments
task_vs_learning_guard.note: Learning outcomes are measured separately from engagement, which is a strength; but no independent no-AI writing transfer test exists.

limitations: High school ESL context, not university academic writing
Homework-only setting does not cover the classroom writing process
suggestions: Extend to university academic writing with classroom writing tasks
Add retention and no-AI transfer assessments

control_group.note: All three studies include a no-AI or traditional-instruction comparison.

randomization.note: Bastani 2025 and Lee 2025 randomized; Marzuki 2024 did not.

pre_test.note: Marzuki has pre/post/delayed tests; Bastani and Lee measure baselines.

post_test.note: Immediate outcome measures present in all studies.

retention_test.note: Only Marzuki 2024 includes a delayed test; Bastani and Lee have none.

transfer_test.note: No study tests independent no-AI writing in a university context; Bastani's independent exam is the closest analogue but in mathematics.

sample_bias.note: Bastani is large; Lee is four classes; Marzuki is a single elite private university.

self_selection.note: Marzuki consent-based; Bastani and Lee randomized.

measurement_validity.note: Task performance is separated from independent performance only in Bastani 2025.

confounders.note: Novelty effects, tool versions and instructor effects not fully controlled across the set.

instructor_effect.note: Marzuki single institution; Lee across four classes; Bastani standardized sessions.

novelty_effect.note: Short interventions in all three studies likely inflate engagement.

tool_version_effect.note: ChatGPT/GPT-4 versions differ across studies and continue to evolve.

ai_usage_policy.note: Only Bastani explicitly contrasts unguarded vs guardrailed usage policies.

task_vs_learning_guard.measured_construct: writing/assignment scores vs independent writing ability
task_vs_learning_guard.note: Writing scores or assignment scores must NOT be equated with independent writing ability. Bastani 2025 shows +48-127% task performance coexisting with -17% independent exam performance; Marzuki's improved writing scores under a ChatGPT-feedback condition carry the same risk of reflecting AI-supported task performance rather than independent writing skill.

limitations: No university-level academic writing RCT measuring independent no-AI writing ability.
Bastani 2025 is methodologically strong but in high school mathematics; subject directness to university academic writing is low.
Lee 2025 is a high school ESL RCT with no retention or transfer test.
Marzuki 2024 is the only writing-context study but lacks randomization, is single-institution, and has no transfer assessment.
suggestions: Design a randomized or matched-section pilot in university academic writing with an independent no-AI writing transfer test.
Adopt guardrail principles from Bastani's GPT Tutor (feedback/hints instead of answers) for the writing context.
Measure process (AI usage logs, reflections) alongside learning and risk outcomes.
Separate task/assignment performance metrics from independent learning metrics in all analyses.
